title: Present perfect 2 + pronouns + no double negatives
title_it: Present perfect 2 (esperienze), pronomi e doppia negazione
goal: Talk about experiences up to now with ever, never, just, already, yet and still, use subject and object pronouns, and avoid double negatives.
goal_it: Parlare di esperienze fino a ora con ever, never, just, already, yet e still, usare i pronomi soggetto e complemento ed evitare la doppia negazione.

steps.title: Present perfect 2: experiences
en: We use the present perfect for experiences up to now, when the exact time does not matter: I have seen that film. Have you ever been to Scotland? The time is open: it is somewhere in your life so far.

Ever means 'at any time in your life' and we use it only in questions. Never means 'not at any time' and it goes with a positive verb: I have never eaten oysters. Short answers: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. / No, I've never eaten them.
Been to means 'visited and come back': I have been to Paris twice. Compare with the past simple, which needs a finished time: I went to Paris last May.
it: Usiamo il present perfect per le esperienze fino a oggi, quando il momento preciso non conta: I have seen that film. Il tempo e' aperto: e' un punto qualsiasi della vita fino a ora.

Ever significa 'mai, in qualsiasi momento della vita' e si usa solo nelle domande. Never significa 'mai' e vuole il verbo positivo: I have never eaten oysters. Risposte brevi: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. / No, I've never eaten them. Attenzione: 'Yes, I've never eaten' e' sbagliato, perche' never e' gia' una negazione.
Been to significa 'sono stato e sono tornato': I have been to Paris twice. Con un momento finito si usa invece il past simple: I went to Paris last May.

head: Present perfect (experience)
Past simple (finished time)
rows: Have you ever eaten Thai food?
Did you eat Thai food yesterday?
I have never been to London.
I went to London last year.
I have eaten Thai food three times this week.
I ate Thai food on Tuesday.

examples.en: Have you ever met a famous person?
examples.it: Hai mai incontrato una persona famosa?

examples.en: She has never flown in a plane.
examples.it: Non ha mai volato in aereo.

examples.en: We have been to Wales twice.
examples.it: Siamo stati in Galles due volte.

steps.title: still, just, already, yet
en: just = a very short time ago: I've just eaten. already = earlier than expected: She has already left. In a question, already shows surprise: Have you already finished?

yet = until now, in questions and negatives, at the end of the sentence: Have you called him yet? I haven't cleaned the room yet. still = continuing, usually before the verb; with a negative it goes before haven't / hasn't: He still hasn't called me.
It's the first time (that) I have ... uses the present perfect: It's the first time I've seen snow. Remember: with yesterday, last night, in 2019 we do NOT use the present perfect.
it: just = appena: I've just eaten. already = gia', prima del previsto: She has already left. Nelle domande already mostra sorpresa: Have you already finished?

yet = finora, fino a ora; si usa nelle domande e nelle negative, in fondo alla frase: Have you called him yet? I haven't cleaned the room yet. still = ancora (continua); di solito prima del verbo, e con la negativa prima di haven't / hasn't: He still hasn't called me.
It's the first time (that) I have ... vuole il present perfect: It's the first time I've seen snow. Ricorda: con yesterday, last night, in 2019 NON si usa il present perfect.

examples.en: It's the first time I've driven on the left.
examples.it: E' la prima volta che guido a sinistra.

steps.title: Subject and object pronouns
en: Subject pronouns come before the verb: I, you, he, she, it, we, you, they. Object pronouns come after a verb or a preposition: me, you, him, her, it, us, you, them.

I saw them at the station. Give it to her. Yesterday I went to the cinema with you. After a preposition we always use an object pronoun, even when there are two people: Sam went with Ana and me (not 'Ana and I' after with).
Common mistake: Me and her went to the shop. Say: She and I went to the shop. Use here for 'qui', there for 'li'' and over there for 'laggiu'': The keys are there, on the table.
it: I pronomi soggetto stanno prima del verbo: I, you, he, she, it, we, you, they. I pronomi complemento stanno dopo un verbo o una preposizione: me, you, him, her, it, us, you, them.
I saw them at the station. Give it to her. Yesterday I went to the cinema with you. Dopo una preposizione si usa sempre il pronome complemento, anche con due persone: Sam went with Ana and me.
Errore tipico: Me and her went to the shop. Si dice: She and I went to the shop. Here = qui, there = li', over there = laggiu': The keys are there, on the table.

examples.en: She called me, but I didn't answer her.
examples.it: Mi ha chiamato, ma non le ho risposto.

examples.en: The bus stop is over there. Let's run to it.
examples.it: La fermata e' laggiu'. Corriamo verso di essa.

steps.title: No double negatives
en: English uses only ONE negative in a clause. With never, nobody, nothing, nowhere the verb stays positive: I never go to the gym (not 'I don't never go'). Nobody called me.

If the verb is negative (haven't, don't, didn't), use any-words: I haven't seen anybody. She didn't say anything. We can't find it anywhere. These mean the same as: I've seen nobody. She said nothing. We can find it nowhere (this form is less usual).
Italian says 'non ho visto nessuno' with two negatives. In English that is a mistake: I haven't seen nobody.
it: In inglese si usa UNA sola negazione per frase. Con never, nobody, nothing, nowhere il verbo resta positivo: I never go to the gym (non 'I don't never go'). Nobody called me.

Se il verbo e' negativo (haven't, don't, didn't), si usano le parole con any: I haven't seen anybody. She didn't say anything. We can't find it anywhere. Significano come: I've seen nobody. She said nothing.
In italiano 'non ho visto nessuno' ha due negazioni. In inglese e' un errore: I haven't seen nobody.

examples.it: Non l'ha ancora detto a nessuno.

steps.q: Have you ___ been to Ireland?
steps.why: Ever is used in questions about experience: Have you ever been to...?
steps.why_it: Ever si usa nelle domande sulle esperienze.

steps.q: Is it correct? 'Yes, I've never eaten sushi.'
options: No, it should be 'No, I've never eaten sushi'
No, it should be 'Yes, I haven't never eaten sushi'
No, it should be 'Yes, I've ever eaten sushi'
steps.why: Never is already a negative, so the short answer starts with No.
steps.why_it: Never e' gia' una negazione, quindi la risposta inizia con No.

steps.q: Maria isn't at home. She ___ (go) to the market and she is still there.
steps.q_it: Maria non e' a casa. E' andata al mercato ed e' ancora li'.
steps.why: Gone means she went and is still there. Been means she went and came back.
steps.why_it: Gone = e' andata ed e' ancora li'.

steps.q: Order the words: a question about experience.
answers: Have you ever visited a castle?
steps.why: Question: have + subject + ever + past participle.
steps.why_it: Domanda: have + soggetto + ever + participio passato.

steps.q: We ___ (eat) pizza three times this week.
steps.q_it: Abbiamo mangiato la pizza tre volte questa settimana.
steps.why: This week is not finished, so the present perfect is natural.
steps.why_it: This week non e' finita: present perfect.

steps.q: They ___ (go) to Wales last weekend.
steps.q_it: Sono andati in Galles lo scorso weekend.
steps.why: Last weekend is finished: past simple.
steps.why_it: Last weekend e' finito: past simple.

steps.q: Order the words.
answers: It's the first time I've flown in a helicopter.
It is the first time I've flown in a helicopter.
steps.why: After 'It's the first time' we use the present perfect.
steps.why_it: Dopo 'It's the first time' si usa il present perfect.

steps.q: Look! Tom ___ arrived. He's at the door now.
steps.why: Just means a very short time ago.
steps.why_it: Just = appena.

steps.q: Have you finished your homework ___?
steps.why: In a question, yet goes at the end.
steps.why_it: Nelle domande yet va in fondo.

steps.q: She ___ hasn't called me. I'm worried.
steps.why: Still before hasn't means it continues: she has not called until now.
steps.why_it: Still prima di hasn't = ancora.

steps.q: I haven't cleaned my room ___.
steps.q_it: Non ho ancora pulito la camera.
steps.why: In a negative, at the end: yet.
steps.why_it: Nella negativa, in fondo: yet.

steps.q: Order the words.
answers: We have already booked the hotel.
steps.why: Already goes between have and the past participle.
steps.why_it: Already sta tra have e il participio.

steps.q: Anna is my friend. I often phone ___.
steps.q_it: Anna e' mia amica. Spesso telefono a ___.
steps.why: After a verb we use the object pronoun: her.
steps.why_it: Dopo il verbo: pronome complemento her.

steps.q: Where are my keys? I can't find ___ anywhere.
steps.why: Keys is plural and it is the object: them.
steps.why_it: Keys e' plurale e complemento: them.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: Luca and I went to the cinema.
Luca and me went to the cinema.
Me and Luca went to the cinema.
Luca and myself went to the cinema.
steps.why: As a subject we use I, and it is polite to put the other person first.
steps.why_it: Come soggetto si usa I; e' educato nominare prima l'altra persona.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: I don't know nothing about it.
I don't never know about it.
steps.why: Only one negative: know nothing, or don't know anything.
steps.why_it: Una sola negazione: know nothing o don't know anything.

steps.q: I haven't met ___ new today. (anybody / nobody)
steps.q_it: Non ho conosciuto nessuno di nuovo oggi.
steps.why: With a negative verb we use any-: anybody / anyone.
steps.why_it: Con il verbo negativo: anybody / anyone.

steps.q: She ___ (never / watch) horror films.
steps.why: Never already makes the sentence negative, so the verb is positive.
steps.why_it: Never rende gia' negativa la frase.

steps.q: Order the words.
answers: Nobody has told me anything about the plan.
Nobody told me anything about the plan.
steps.why: Nobody is the negative, so told me anything is positive in form.
steps.why_it: Nobody e' la negazione.

steps.q: Review. Right now my sister ___ a shower, so please wait.
steps.q_it: Ripasso. In questo momento mia sorella ___ la doccia.
steps.why: Right now = present continuous.
steps.why_it: Right now = present continuous.

steps.q: Review. I usually get up at seven, but yesterday I ___ (get) up at nine.
steps.q_it: Di solito mi alzo alle sette, ma ieri alle nove.
steps.why: Yesterday is a finished time: past simple. (Usually = present simple.)
steps.why_it: Yesterday e' un momento finito: past simple. (Usually = present simple.)

steps.q: Review. We ___ dinner when the lights went out.
steps.q_it: Ripasso. Stavamo cenando quando se n'e' andata la luce.
steps.why: An action in progress interrupted by a shorter one: past continuous.
steps.why_it: Azione in corso interrotta: past continuous.

steps.q: Review. I ___ (lose) my phone, so I can't call you now.
steps.q_it: Ho perso il telefono, quindi non posso chiamarti.
steps.why: A past action with a result now: present perfect.
steps.why_it: Azione passata con risultato adesso: present perfect.

steps.q: Review. Which sentence is correct?
steps.why: Yesterday is a finished time: past simple, not present perfect.
steps.why_it: Yesterday = past simple.

steps.q: Review. While I ___ the dishes, the phone rang.
steps.q_it: Ripasso. Mentre ___ i piatti, ha squillato il telefono.
steps.why: While + a longer action in progress: past continuous.
steps.why_it: While + azione in corso: past continuous.

steps.q: Review. Order the words.
answers: She is studying now because she has an exam tomorrow.
steps.why: Now = present continuous; has an exam = present simple (state).
steps.why_it: Now = present continuous; has = present simple.

cards.ex: Have you ever been to London?
We have been to Spain twice.
It's the first time I've cooked for ten people.
Nothing happened. I haven't been anywhere.
